record_identity.title: Railway cloud platform intrusion and customer environment-variable exposure

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Railway October 2026 platform intrusion and credential exposure
incident_identity.date_basis: Railway's 10 November follow-up dates attacker dummy-account signup/probing from 18 October (initial attempts unsuccessful), the first successful build-isolation escape to 20 October 07:28 UTC, loss of access to customer data by 21 October 09:25 UTC, and confirmation of removal from internal systems by 22 October 03:32 UTC. This is a bounded campaign and response interval, not continuous successful access.

summary: From 18 to 22 October 2026, attackers probed and then breached Railway, a cloud platform for deploying applications. On 20 October, they escaped part of a build system's isolation, stole an internal credential and obtained portions of Railway's source code. After Railway blocked that path, the attackers exploited a separate cloud-permission error to access further credentials, query customer environment variables and decrypt some of them. Railway says at most 1.85% of workspaces, around 100,000, could have had variables decrypted; this is an upper bound, not a confirmed victim count. Compromised data also included linked-account tokens belonging to 1,852 users, and Railway estimated around US$740,000 in unauthorised spending with stolen API keys. Railway twice stopped new builds, revoked credentials and rebuilt affected systems; existing customer applications kept running. Railway's later investigation described rapid parallel attack exploration involving safeguards-removed AI models and agent fan-outs, while leaving specific model actions and their human direction unverified.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Railway's 10 November detailed report supersedes important timing and access uncertainties in its 21–22 October preliminary disclosures. Railway states that unsuccessful account probing began on 18 October; a partial build-filesystem isolation escape at 07:28 UTC on 20 October exposed a build credential, which allowed access to Temporal build histories and an internal monorepo snapshot. Subsequent source-code inspection and an erroneously scoped OIDC cloud-trust configuration enabled acquisition of cloud credentials, further internal credentials, access to the environment-variable database and decryption via a key management service on 21 October. Decryption began at 04:42 UTC, not after the 05:27 time implied by the preliminary sequence. Railway identifies a maximum of 1.85% (~100,000) potentially affected workspaces, separately reports linked-account tokens of 1,852 users and estimates about US$740,000 in unauthorised spending on stolen API keys. It reports no customer repository snapshot downloads and no account logins using stolen credentials. Railway describes attacker use of abliterated models and agent fan-outs in rapid parallel exploration; the publicly released evidence does not show model instructions, per-action selection, operator control transfers or independently verified inference-trace detail. Railway confirms containment and staged restoration, while hosted customer applications remained online. Wiz's other AI-platform cases remain contextual and are not merged into this incident.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The materialised mechanism was a multi-step external intrusion exploiting build isolation and overly broad internal credential trust, then accessing protected environment variables and linked account tokens. Railway's detailed account strengthens the evidence that the attacker used AI-assisted rapid exploration but still cannot attribute each exploit choice, privileged access or exfiltration action to an identifiable model or agent rather than the human operator. That distinction keeps Fidelity Class findings unresolved while preserving the supported confidentiality, service disruption and financial consequences. Railway's own monitoring, emergency shutdown, revocation and rebuild are defender response, not successful Fidelity Class mappings to the attacking system.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case illustrates how build credentials, stored workflow history, internal source code and cloud trust configuration can form a cumulative escalation route. Railway's expanded account also shows why materialised protected-data access and unauthorised AI-key spending can be assessed separately from the unresolved allocation of decisions between attacker and AI tooling.
assessment_boundaries: The detailed 10 November Railway report supersedes key preliminary timings and discloses exploit-chain structure, but the external forensic review, underlying network logs and attacker-model traces remain unavailable.

Railway now describes abliterated models and attacker agent fan-outs; this is a first-party model-use attribution without published agent prompts, model identity, permitted scope or per-action human/AI decision history.
No evidence establishes that Railway's own customer-facing AI assistant caused this breach.
At most 1.85% (approximately 100,000) potentially affected workspaces is a ceiling on environments with possible decrypted variables, not the number of confirmed decrypted keys or individuals.
Railway separately states that linked account tokens of 1,852 users were included; that token count must not be conflated with the 100,000-workspace upper bound or account logins.
Railway confirms attacker access to its own internal monorepo and 353 stored build histories, but says it found no indication of customer repository snapshot downloads or customer database access.
Railway's approximately US$740,000 unauthorised AI-key spend estimate is a reported financial consequence, distinct from unknown eventual refunds and any conjectured model-distillation proceeds.
Provider hypotheses about key resale or downstream distillation do not establish successful distillation or identify a downstream model provider as a breached target in this occurrence.
Railway's defender controls and service recovery do not supply independent positive mappings to the attacking AI system.
Other October AI-developer platform attacks remain contextual; no common attacker, shared exploit mechanism or agent is established merely from similarity.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Source-first chronology reconciled against Railway's more detailed 10 November report, retaining provider-reported AI involvement while withholding model-specific Fidelity Class findings and preserving defender separation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 20 October at 13:58 UTC Railway's monitoring paged the on-call engineer for anomalous latency, beginning investigation.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Detection was an observed platform response; the hostile model or agent, if any, was not yet identified.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 20 October at 07:28 UTC the attacker partly escaped isolation in Railway's build environment, obtained a credential and used access beyond the credential's intended registry-push task; Railway halted builds during its response.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A real authorisation boundary was attacked, but the public record does not identify the AI system's task choices or control over that attempt.
clauses.adjudication_note: Necessary model/agent attribution and per-action authorisation evidence are absent; the human actor's unauthorised intrusion alone is not an AI Fidelity Class mapping.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The real build-system privilege escalation potentially engages authority-boundary integrity only if the suspected AI operated the relevant tool pathway. The published report does not identify an AI action, authorised task, available permissions or human control of the attempt.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway initially assessed the exploit as remediated during the evening of 20 October, then identified an additional capability for broader privilege escalation at 19:53 UTC and resumed containment.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An initial containment conclusion proved incomplete; subsequent compromise was not automatically a failure by an AI agent.

clauses.source_paraphrase: After access to Temporal build histories and Railway's internal monorepo, the attacker found an erroneously configured OIDC cloud-trust binding, obtained short-lived and longer-lived internal credentials, and used an SSH-enabled internal orchestration machine to reach protected data.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Sensitive build and credential boundaries were crossed in the confirmed human/adversary intrusion; no separate agent-selected tool action is publicly demonstrated.
clauses.adjudication_note: Attacker-side AI involvement is suspected but the agent execution and credential-access sequence are not attributed to a specific AI system.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Exfiltration of CI credentials and later access to credential-bearing artifacts are evidenced for the attacker. Whether an AI system accessed, selected or transferred those authentication materials is not demonstrated by the public report.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway's 10 November forensics show that the attacker retrieved encrypted customer variable envelopes and used compromised KMS credentials to decrypt some between 04:42 and 07:15 UTC on 21 October; the upper bound on possibly affected workspaces was 1.85%.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Real non-public customer information was accessed; the upper-bound potentially affected workspace count must not be treated as a confirmed decrypted-key or victim count.
clauses.adjudication_note: The protected-information compromise is supported as an external attack; AI-specific execution and choice of access are not established.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The customer-variable access and partial decryption are supported. The action has not been attributed to the suspected AI models, so no AI-system protected-information access finding can yet be resolved.

clauses.source_paraphrase: By 09:25 UTC on 21 October Railway had inspected attacker-payload logs indicating sought API-key names and informed providers including GitHub, GitLab and AI inference vendors to revoke potentially exposed credentials.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reported targeting of AI keys is evidence of attacker objective; the revocation is a defender action with uncertain per-key need, not evidence of autonomous model intent or a successful attacking-agent safeguard.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway and its status page reported platform-wide build pauses and periods of API, dashboard, CLI and support disruption during containment; running customer deployments stayed online.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The response caused documented important-workflow unavailability while existing workloads remained accessible; distinguish the harm from the protective intervention and its intended scope.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway reported no access to customer data after 21 October 09:25 UTC, later confirmed complete expulsion from internal systems by 22 October 03:32 UTC, and restored build functionality in stages. These are distinct detection and validation milestones.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Defensive recovery and containment occurred, but the reported control effect is not classified as the attacker AI system's positive behaviour.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway's 10 November account describes rapid parallel exploit exploration using agent fan-outs, safeguards-removed models and a harness compared to ARTEX, and attributes targeting of AI-provider credentials to observed attacker queries. The provider has not released model-session or operator-command traces.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The expanded evidence supports provider-reported AI-assisted capability in the attack, but does not isolate model-selected decisions, permissions or transfers of control for a formal attacker-AI conduct finding.
clauses.adjudication_note: Railway's stronger attribution justifies a targeted FC recognition review, but human versus AI choices and specific model outputs are still undisclosed.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Railway now reports the use of AI agents in parallel exploit exploration, but the publicly available account does not distinguish attacker instructions, agent-selected exploits or subsequent control transfers for each operation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The company placed the upper bound of potentially compromised workspaces at 1.85%, about 100,000; it did not claim every such workspace had secrets decrypted. A wider set of users saw credential resets as a precaution.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Potential exposure and precautionary revocation population differ from established data access and confirmed affected people; no source permits their arithmetic conflation.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Independent cloud-security researchers included Railway in a cluster of October incidents affecting AI-development platforms, without establishing common control of all events.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Contextual similarity and industry-level reporting do not establish shared actor identity or justify merging distinct platform breaches.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway found that attacker-created dummy accounts and unsuccessful probing started on 18 October, before the first successful build-isolation escape on 20 October.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Preparatory unsuccessful attempts belong to the same bounded campaign but are not proof of earlier successful penetration or autonomous agent behaviour.

clauses.source_paraphrase: A compromised build credential exposed histories of 353 builds and a snapshot of Railway's own internal monorepo; Railway reports no evidence of downloading customer repository snapshots.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The reported privileged source and workflow-history access informed subsequent escalation, but the model's specific retrieval decisions and customer-repository access cannot be inferred.
clauses.adjudication_note: Real attacker access is supported, but an attributable AI-system data-access choice is not established by the published forensic report.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Access to protected build-history and internal source data is documented for the attacker; the publication does not establish whether the AI tools themselves selected or performed that access.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Railway reported linked-account tokens for 1,852 users within the affected data and estimated approximately US$740,000 of unauthorised spending with stolen AI-provider keys; it described refund efforts.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Confirmed credential exposure and estimated realised spend are distinct materialised consequences; neither proves who selected individual transactions or that downstream model distillation succeeded.

system_context.specific_model_or_runtime: Railway's 10 November report attributes rapid parallel attacker exploration to safeguards-removed models and agent fan-outs; specific models, tool harness traces and operator inputs are not disclosed.
system_context.interface_surface: Reported adversarial AI-assisted exploit exploration against Railway's live build, Temporal and cloud environments; exact model tools, commands, intermediate instructions and decision allocations not public.

agent_context.evidence_basis: Railway's detailed report describes AI-assisted agent fan-outs and abliterated model use, without publishing identifiable runtime execution traces, confirmed agent counts or independently model-selected action sequences.

occurrence_environment.environment_detail: Railway confirms a live external compromise and describes the attacker's AI-assisted exploit exploration; no public execution trace resolves the deployed agent runtime or independently selected tool operations.
occurrence_environment.evidence_basis: Real production intrusion, exposure and AI-assisted attack attribution are first-party reported; individual model choices and operator direction remain unresolved.

entities.evidence_basis: The provider reported unauthorised access to its internal infrastructure and temporary disruption of its dashboard, API and build services.

entities.evidence_basis: Railway's own report describes decrypted customer environment variables and a bounded potential workspace-exposure ceiling; it does not establish every customer's exposure.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: The 10 November report adds first-party attribution of attacker AI-assisted parallel exploitation and stronger evidence of real credential, internal-source and protected-variable compromise. It does not publish model/agent execution traces, permitted task scopes or per-action allocation of human and synthetic direction. Human-initiated attack conduct and Railway's own defensive controls are not by themselves AI Fidelity Class results. FC-025, FC-064, FC-089 and FC-090 remain noncanonical candidates; a targeted, current-class recognition review remains open.

aggregate_harm_screening.rationale: The bounded Railway incident materialised confidentiality, financial and significant development-service consequences. The maximum potentially exposed workspace population is not assumed to have been actually compromised.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve HIM dimensions screened against Railway's 10 November first-party detailed report. Confirmed protected-data and linked-token access supports S2 privacy; the estimated US$740,000 unauthorised key spend supports S2 financial-economic, subject to recovery uncertainty; prolonged build and API service disruption supports S3. The 100,000-workspace figure is only an exposure upper bound, and existing hosted applications stayed online.
